_comment: Link prospects, per site. Every entry is a place a real business could legitimately appear: a trade association it could join, a chamber it could belong to, a supplier whose dealer directory it qualifies for, or a page that already mentions it without linking. Nothing here is a link to be bought, spun or blasted, and nothing is sent automatically. scripts/link-prospects.mjs verifies and drafts; a person sends.
_status_values: candidate (found, not assessed) | qualified (worth pursuing) | drafted (outreach written, unsent) | sent (a human sent it) | won (link live) | declined (they said no) | unsuitable (we were wrong about it)
_on_cost: Association and chamber listings usually cost money. That makes them a business decision about membership, not a link tactic, so cost is recorded on every prospect and never hidden. A link that costs $500 a year may still be worth it for the referrals, but nobody should discover the price after deciding.

prospects.why: The fencing industry's main US professional body, ~1,500 member companies, and it runs a contractor locator members are listed in. Genuine trade relevance rather than a generic directory.
Regional chapters are usually easier to join and more locally relevant than the national body. Worth checking whether a Louisiana or Gulf States chapter exists before pursuing national membership.
Trade-specific fence contractor directory. Assess quality before pursuing — check whether listings are editorially reviewed or simply accepted, since an open directory is worth very little.
Second fence trade body. Assess against AFA rather than joining both by default.

State-level association for exactly this trade in exactly this state, with a public member directory carrying contact details. The strongest single prospect on this list: relevant, local, and the directory is the membership benefit rather than an afterthought.

prospects.org: Towing and Recovery Association of America
prospects.why: National towing body. Members get a listing in the online directory and the annual buyers' guide. Less locally relevant than TTSA, so pursue second.

discovery._comment: Searches that find more prospects. Discovery needs a search engine, which this repo has no key for and should not get one just for this — run these by hand or with an agent, then add what they turn up as prospects above. The verifying and drafting either side of that IS automated.
_patterns: "<business name>" -site:<domain>            → mentions that may not link
<city> chamber of commerce membership          → local chambers
<manufacturer> "find a dealer" OR "find an installer"  → supplier directories
